stem: Let $X=\{{=a}, {=b}, {=c}\}$ and $Y=\{y : y\in N, 1\le y\le {=M}\}$ where N is the set of natural numbers. The relation $R$ from $X$ to $Y$ is defined by $x\,R\,y$ where $y={=m}x$. Show that $R$ is a function from $X$ to $Y$, then find how many elements of the codomain $Y$ do not belong to the range.
solution: $R=\{({=a}, {=m*a}), ({=b}, {=m*b}), ({=c}, {=m*c})\}$. Each element of $X$ has exactly one arrow to an element of $Y$, so $R$ is a function.
The range $=\{{=m*a}, {=m*b}, {=m*c}\}$, which has 3 elements and is a subset of $Y$.
Elements of $Y$ not in the range: ${=M}-3={=M-3}$.
notes: Max image m*(a+2) < M so range is within Y; range always has 3 distinct elements.
